egypt.finding: The central bank raised rates by 100 basis points after Thursday's close to defend the pound, which is down 8% against the dollar in a month, mostly for local reasons. The EGX30 rose 0.6% to 49,596 as Banque du Caire's offering was executed.

helped.name: Banks: CIB, EFG Holding
helped.why: High rates protect lending margins and T-bill income. CIB rose 0.5% on Thursday and is 17% up this year.

helped.name: Dollar earners: Orascom, Elsewedy
helped.why: A weaker pound lifts the pound value of dollar revenue; the dollar is up 8% against the pound in a month.

helped.name: Ports: Alexandria Containers
helped.why: Up 1.5% on Thursday and 29% this year; momentum, not news, so the call is weak.

hurt.name: Developers: Talaat Moustafa, Palm Hills
hurt.why: Higher rates raise buyers' financing costs; Talaat Moustafa is down 8% in a month and flat this year.

hurt.name: Telecom Egypt
hurt.why: Down 1.7% on Thursday and 11% in a month after an 83% run this year; profit-taking, with no news beyond setting a date for its third-quarter results.

hurt.name: Fertilisers: Abu Qir
hurt.why: Down 3.5%, the worst of the 12 Egyptian stocks on Thursday, even as it reported nine-month profit roughly doubling to about EGP 13bn: profit-taking after a 73% run this year, with the results largely expected.

egypt.stocksNote: Worst on Thursday: Abu Qir −3.5%, despite nine-month profit roughly doubling. Best: Alexandria Containers +1.5%.

week.event: EGX reopens after the rate hike
week.why: The first session to price Thursday's 100 bps hike; watch banks and developers in the first hour.
Retail tranche 27 times covered at EGP 5.30; retail buyers can sell back at the offer price for 30 days, which cushions the debut.
The figure the central bank answers to; a rise keeps the case for high rates.

views.call: The hike supports the pound and the banks
views.note: From 30 Oct: USD/EGP 56.04, CIB EGP 120.47, EGX30 49,596. Wrong if the dollar closes above EGP 57 before the next T-bill auction.

views.call: Developers lag while rates stay high
views.note: From 30 Oct: Talaat Moustafa EGP 80.40, Palm Hills EGP 11.40, against the EGX30 at 49,596; judged over four weeks.

views.call: Oil above $110 weighs on the pound
views.note: From 30 Oct: Brent $114.88. Wrong if Brent falls below $100.

flows.title: Who bought and who sold
flows.sub: Net EGX equity flows, Thu 29 Oct, EGP bn · Youm7, Masr Times, Newsroom
flows.read: Dominated by the execution of Banque du Caire's EGP 36.4 bn offering: foreign institutions bought, Egyptian institutions sold. Read normal days' flows, not this one, for who is backing the market.
flows.source: Youm7, Masr Times and Newsroom, which agree to the decimal; Alam Al-Mal's differing figures are ruled out because its buy and sell values exceed the session's EGP 43.9bn turnover.

calls.headline: The central bank hikes to defend the pound
calls.body: The Monetary Policy Committee raised all key rates by 100 basis points after Thursday's close, taking the overnight deposit rate to 20.00% and lending to 21.00%, the first rise since March 2024. Most analysts had expected a hold. The dollar is up 8% against the pound in a month but only 0.8% against major currencies, so about 90% of the move is local: the hike is aimed at bringing back the foreign money that sold Egyptian debt.
calls.view: Supportive for the pound and the banks, negative for developers. Sunday is the first session to price the hike.
calls.moves: CIB and EFG Holding gain on wider margins; Talaat Moustafa and Palm Hills lose on dearer financing for buyers.
calls.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 57 before the next T-bill auction, or the auction's average yield falls.

calls.headline: Banque du Caire's offering pulls in money, but distorts the flows
calls.body: The state lender's retail tranche closed about 27 times covered, with orders for about 9.29 billion shares against 343.1 million offered. Thursday's execution put foreign institutions EGP 29.2bn net buyers and Egyptian institutions EGP 34.3bn net sellers, figures driven by the offering rather than the market. Enppi is next, planned for the second half of January.
calls.view: Strong demand for state offerings is a good sign for the programme and for brokers' fees, but Thursday's flows say nothing about who is backing the EGX30.
calls.moves: EFG Holding gains from a busier offering pipeline; CIB and other listed banks face a new rival for investors' money.
calls.wrong: Banque du Caire trades below its offer price in its first week, or Enppi's listing slips past January.

calls.headline: Oil at $115 widens Egypt's import bill
calls.body: Brent settled at $114.88 a barrel, within 3% of its 52-week high and up about 89% this year, and December Brent was near $116 on Friday after the Revolutionary Guards said four tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Egypt buys much of its fuel abroad, so every dollar on the barrel adds to the dollars it needs.
calls.view: A drag on the pound as long as Brent holds above $110; it adds to the case for the rate hike rather than against it.
calls.moves: Abu Qir Fertilizers and other exporters with dollar sales are cushioned; consumer companies with imported inputs, such as Juhayna, face higher costs.
calls.wrong: Brent falls below $100, for example on a de-escalation in the Gulf.

global.finding: Alphabet's 12.6% fall on its results pulled the Nasdaq 1.4% lower; Walmart and JPMorgan rose as money moved to steadier names.

close.title: Thursday's close
close.note: A dash is a figure not confirmed by two sources this morning: Brent's and gold's day changes differ between sources, and the dollar index was not confirmed.

helped.name: Retail and staples: Walmart
helped.why: Up 2.1% on Thursday as money left tech; steady earnings are in demand while AI payback is questioned.

helped.name: Banks: JPMorgan
helped.why: Up 1.3%; higher-for-longer rates keep lending margins wide.

helped.name: Energy: Exxon Mobil
helped.why: Up 0.7% and 51% this year with Brent above $110; the oil price, not the day's news, drives it.

hurt.name: Search and ads: Alphabet
hurt.why: Down 12.6%: AI Mode is eating into search advertising faster than expected, and free cash flow turned negative.

hurt.name: Cloud spenders: Amazon
hurt.why: Down 4.3% in sympathy ahead of its own results; the same AI-spending question hangs over it.

hurt.name: AI chips: Broadcom, Nvidia
hurt.why: Down 1.9% and 0.8%; if the spenders slow, the chip makers' orders follow.

week.why: Control of Congress shapes spending and tariff policy; markets can swing on the result.
After Alphabet's and Amazon's misses, the next test of big tech's earnings.
Strong growth and 3.6% PCE inflation keep a hike in play; a hike lifts the dollar, which presses on the pound.

views.call: Money rotates from AI spenders to steady earners
views.note: From 30 Oct: Walmart $121.25, JPMorgan $343.58, Alphabet $283.82; judged over four weeks.

views.call: Amazon trades lower after its miss
views.note: From 30 Oct: closed at $243.79 before results, about 6% lower after hours. Wrong if it closes back above $245 within two weeks.

calls.headline: Alphabet's AI-search miss hits big tech
calls.body: Alphabet fell 12.6% after revenue missed and free cash flow turned negative, as AI Mode slowed search advertising. Amazon lost 4.3% and the Nasdaq 1.4%, while Walmart (+2.1%), JPMorgan (+1.3%) and Exxon (+0.7%) rose: money moved from AI spenders to steadier earnings.
calls.view: Cautious on ad-funded and AI-heavy tech into Amazon's and Apple's results; the market is now asking for AI spending to pay back, not just to grow.
calls.moves: Alphabet, Amazon and Broadcom most exposed; Walmart, JPMorgan and Berkshire as places money hides.
calls.wrong: Alphabet recovers half its fall within a week, or the Nasdaq makes a new high before November's US inflation figure.
calls.notice: Results dates for Apple and Amazon conflict between reports; check them before relying on the week ahead.

calls.headline: Amazon and Intel misses deepen the AI-spending sell-off
calls.body: After the bell, Amazon reported earnings of $1.89 a share against $1.97 expected and revenue of $201.9bn against $202.2bn, and fell about 6%. Intel beat on adjusted earnings but missed on revenue at $16.5bn, and dropped 17% to 20% in extended trading.
calls.view: Expect the Nasdaq to stay under pressure into Monday; the market is punishing any AI spender that does not show the spending paying back.
calls.moves: Amazon, Nvidia and Broadcom are most exposed; Walmart and JPMorgan benefit from the rotation.
calls.wrong: The Nasdaq recovers Thursday's loss within the week.

calls.headline: Strong growth and sticky inflation keep a December Fed hike in play
calls.body: US growth accelerated to 3.4% in the third quarter, above the 3.2% expected, and annual PCE inflation came in at 3.6%, with the core measure at 3.1%. The 10-year Treasury yield stayed near 5%.
calls.view: Higher-for-longer rates favour banks and weigh on the most expensive growth stocks; they also keep pressure on emerging-market currencies, the pound included.
calls.moves: JPMorgan and Berkshire Hathaway gain; Tesla and Nvidia, the highest-valued, are most exposed.
calls.wrong: The 10-year yield falls below 4.75% before the Fed's December meeting.

egx.finding: The EGX30 rose 0.6% to 49,596 on Thursday, with the rate hike announced after the close; Alexandria Containers and Juhayna led the 12 Egyptian stocks, Abu Qir Fertilizers lagged.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: Thursday’s 100 bps hike raises what banks earn on loans and T-bills, which they hold in size, faster than it raises their deposit costs. CIB and EFG trade 8% and 6% below their 50-day averages, so little of this is priced in.

sectors.name: Investment banks and brokers
sectors.why: Banque du Caire’s retail tranche was 27 times covered and the state plans to list Enppi in January: more offerings mean more fees and more trading.

sectors.name: Dollar earners: contractors, cables, fertilisers
sectors.why: The dollar is 8% higher against the pound in a month, which lifts the pound value of export and overseas revenue at Orascom, Elsewedy and Abu Qir.

stocks.why: A return to its 50-day average (130.7). The hike widens margins, the stock is 16% below its 52-week high, and it trades near 5.5 times its last reported earnings.
stocks.wrong: it closes below EGP 114, 5% under Thursday’s close, or the EGX30 falls while it does.

stocks.why: Dollar revenue from Gulf and US projects gains from the weaker pound. Up 91% this year, so a pause is as likely as a new high.
stocks.wrong: it closes below EGP 780, 5% under Thursday, or the pound recovers sharply.

sectors.name: Real estate developers
sectors.why: Dearer financing hits instalment buyers and developers’ own borrowing at once. Talaat Moustafa and Palm Hills are 12% and 16% below their 50-day averages and still falling, with both at their lowest since April. Talaat Moustafa's EGP 11 trillion state deal and Al Ahly Pharos' Palm Hills valuation are the counterweights, so confidence is medium.

sectors.name: Food and consumer
sectors.why: A weaker pound raises the cost of imported inputs such as milk powder and packaging; companies with pricing power, like Juhayna, pass it on with a lag.

stocks.why: Down 7.6% in a month and 12% under its 50-day average (91.3); the hike lands on its buyers and its debt. Its EGP 11 trillion state deal is a long-term offset, so confidence is low.
stocks.wrong: it closes back above EGP 88, near its 50-day average, or a big sales launch beats expectations.

stocks.why: Down 10.6% in a month and 16% under its 50-day average (13.5), under the same rate pressure as Talaat Moustafa. Al Ahly Pharos values it at EGP 21.40 on existing assets alone, which argues against a deep fall.

Profit-taking after a 73% run this year: it fell 3.5% on Thursday even as nine-month profit roughly doubled to about EGP 13bn, a sign the good news was priced in. The weaker pound helps its exports, so the downside should be limited.
stocks.wrong: it makes a new high above EGP 95.75.

news.headline: Talaat Moustafa signs EGP 11 trillion development deal with the state
news.text: Four mixed-use projects in East Cairo, Alexandria and the North Coast over more than 37 million square metres; the president asked for 200,000 rental homes on top.

news.headline: Abu Qir Fertilizers' nine-month profit roughly doubles to EGP 13bn
news.text: Unaudited results to September show profit of about EGP 12.97bn, helped by steadier gas supplies; the board also approved a McKinsey strategy from fiscal 2027.

news.headline: Al Ahly Pharos values Palm Hills at EGP 21.40
news.text: The fair value, based on existing assets alone, is about 74% above the price when it was published.

news.headline: Banque du Caire's retail tranche 27 times covered
news.text: Orders reached about 9.29 billion shares against 343.1 million offered, so applicants get about 3.7% of what they asked for. The Cabinet has approved the sale of a 30% to 45% stake.

news.headline: Enppi to list in the second half of January
news.text: The state plans to sell 10% to 20% of the engineering contractor, priced in dollars, as part of a push to raise dollar inflows before the IMF programme ends.

news.headline: MNT-Halan's EGP 4bn injection into its Egyptian unit is fully paid
news.text: 163.27 million shares were bought at EGP 24.50, lifting the unit's issued capital to EGP 176.3m.

egp.finding: The dollar is at EGP 56.04, near its 52-week high, after foreign investors sold local debt; Thursday's 100-basis-point hike is the central bank's answer.

drivers.name: Rates raised 100 bps
drivers.why: Deposit 20.00%, lending 21.00% on Thursday, the first rise since March 2024. Higher yields are meant to bring back the carry-trade money that left in October.

drivers.name: Foreign sales of local debt
drivers.why: Portfolio investors sold Egyptian treasuries as the dollar crossed 55 and then 56. Watch the next T-bill auction for whether demand returns.

drivers.name: IMF eighth and final review
drivers.why: The mission is in Cairo. A passed review releases the last tranche and steadies inflows; a delay would weigh on the pound.

drivers.name: Oil at $115
drivers.why: Brent near its 52-week high raises Egypt's fuel import bill, adding to dollar demand.

view.headline: The hike should cap the dollar near 56.5 for now
view.body: A 100-basis-point rise lifts T-bill yields back above inflation and pays foreign holders to stay. Most of the month's move was local, as the Pound or dollar chart shows.
view.moves: CIB and EFG Holding gain on wider margins and inflows; Talaat Moustafa and Palm Hills lose on dearer mortgages.
view.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 57 before the next auction, or the auction's average yield falls rather than rises.

news.headline: Central bank raises key rates by 100 basis points
news.text: The overnight deposit rate rises to 20.00% and the lending rate to 21.00%, with the main operation and discount rates at 20.50%: the first increase since March 2024. Most analysts had expected a hold.

news.headline: EFG Hermes: about $7bn of foreign money left Egyptian debt in three weeks
news.text: EFG Hermes research estimates net portfolio outflows of about $7bn over the past three weeks, as the pound fell about 7% against the dollar amid regional tension and higher oil prices.

news.headline: IMF mission starts the final review
news.text: The mission is in Cairo for the eighth and last review of Egypt's $8bn Extended Fund Facility; a passed review releases the final tranche.

us.finding: Alphabet's 12.6% fall pulled the Nasdaq down 1.4%; the S&P 500 lost 0.3% and the Dow 0.3%, while Walmart and JPMorgan rose as money moved to steadier earnings.

afterBell.name: Intel

sectors.name: Banks

sectors.name: Steady earners
sectors.why: Money left AI spenders for predictable earnings on Thursday; Walmart is up 17% in a month. Rotations like this can reverse quickly.

stocks.wrong: Brent falls below $100, for example on a Gulf de-escalation.

stocks.why: Well above its 50-day average (109.8) after the rotation; its 52-week high of 134.20 is the ceiling to watch.
stocks.wrong: it closes below $115 as money returns to tech.

sectors.name: Big AI spenders

sectors.name: Highly valued growth
sectors.why: A 10-year yield near 5% lowers what future profits are worth today, which weighs most on the most expensive stocks.

stocks.why: Missed on earnings ($1.89 against $1.97) and revenue, and fell about 6% after hours, which would take it near 229.
stocks.wrong: it closes back above $245 within two weeks of the results.

stocks.why: Already down 17.5% in a month and near its 52-week low (273.50), so much of the bad news is in the price; the risk is further downgrades.

news.headline: Alphabet suffers its worst day, losing about $500bn
news.text: Alphabet fell 12.6% to $283.82 after revenue missed estimates and an executive said Google's AI Mode produced fewer ads. Adjusted earnings were $2.67 a share against an expected $3.02.

news.headline: Amazon and Intel fall after the bell
news.text: Amazon missed on earnings and revenue and fell about 6% in extended trading; Intel beat on earnings but missed on revenue and fell sharply.

news.headline: US growth hits 3.4% as PCE inflation stays at 3.6%
news.text: Third-quarter growth beat the 3.2% expected and core PCE rose 3.1%, supporting bets on another Fed hike in December.

news.headline: ExxonMobil's profit doubles to $15.4bn
news.text: Third-quarter revenue rose about 33% to $113.2bn on higher oil prices and record output, beating estimates.

news.headline: Microsoft lines up $25bn bond sale for AI
news.text: Its first bond sale since 2017, a sign of what AI spending now costs even the most cash-rich companies.

global.finding: Brent held near $115 on Gulf shipping risk, gold slipped toward $4,000 as US yields stayed near 5%, and Bitcoin fell.

notes.brent: Egypt imports fuel, so a dearer barrel widens the import bill and adds to dollar demand; Gulf producers' cash, and their investment in Egypt, rises with it.
notes.gold_usd: Sets the base for Egyptian gold prices; Egyptians buy gold as a hedge against the pound, so local demand stays strong even as the world price falls.
notes.dxy: A stronger dollar pressures emerging-market currencies and pulls money out of their debt, Egypt's included.
notes.btc: A gauge of risk appetite; when it falls with tech stocks, investors are cutting risk, which rarely helps frontier markets.

news.headline: Brent near $116 after Hormuz mine claims
news.text: December Brent rose toward $116 on Friday after the Revolutionary Guards said four tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz; Brent settled at $114.88 on Thursday.

news.headline: Gold falls on strong US growth and inflation
news.text: Spot gold fell about 1% to roughly $4,025 an ounce as the GDP and inflation figures supported bets on Fed tightening.
